items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I remember conversations... Bill Evans is here. Wow, cool, let’s go.

ctx.x: Is there any kind of discrimination with the age of musicians these days that are landing on those kind of labels do you think? © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

I think there probably is. I think, I would almost bet that yeah. Like if I wanted to go to another label right now at my age, I might be able to land a deal with somebody, somebody might give me a shot, because I’ve got a proven track record. But an older musician trying to, who isn’t as established, probably wouldn’t get a deal. No I think there’s a tendency towards the brand new and terrific you know, or brand new. Who says whether it’s terrific or not. I mean there’s lots of young, brand new talent. I mean…
